title: Fit to content, host half: drag a member, parent redraws itself
summary: Zach's second success criterion — drag a free-layout member around inside a Block, in a real React Flow AND a real tldraw canvas, and watch the parent auto-fit around it live, non-buggy, with a mutation-verified reentrancy story rather than a hand-waved "it converges".
intro: The plain-DOM half of this ask (port view / expanded view / ports offset vs inline / a crowded-rail bug demo, all before-and-after in one story) already shipped as FitToContent.stories.tsx from a prior lane — confirmed still green, untouched, 59/59 of its own stories passing before this lane added a line. This lane is the host half: drag a real child member inside a real React Flow node and a real tldraw shape, and have the parent's box grow and shrink around it while the gesture is still in flight — not just at release.

Neither host file changed. reactFlowHost.tsx and tldrawHost.tsx are byte-identical to the tip this lane started from. A membersLayout: "free" node is still just a type: "block" node to both engines — the drag, the auto-fit, and the reentrancy guard all live in the shared src/hosts/nodeViews.tsx translation layer three new/changed files feed. That is the concrete shape of “the host owns the box, the box drives the wiring”: dragging works under either engine for free.

PieceWhat it doesWhere
The mathblockExpandedFitHeight, resolveBlockHeight — landed by a prior lane, untouched heresrc/layout/fitToContent.ts
The dragPlain pointer capture bounded to the member's own box — one boundary, one active id, like blockMembers.tsx's own stack-mode dnd-kit boundary but answering a continuous (x, y) instead of a reorderhosts/memberDrag.ts, new
The fitMeasures chrome + member rects, calls the landed math, carries the reentrancy latchhosts/blockAutoFit.ts, new
The wiringBlockNodeView composes the two, moveMember writes a settled drag back into the scenehosts/nodeViews.tsx, additive edit
changes: apps/storybook-basics/src/hosts/memberDrag.ts — new. useFreeMemberDrag: plain PointerEvent + setPointerCapture, one boundary per members region, at most one member dragging at a time. Live position is ephemeral (drives a continuous re-fit); the scene is written once, at release — this repo's own established idiom (reactFlowHost.tsx's NodeResizer.onResizeEnd, tldrawHost.tsx's onTranslateEnd/onResizeEnd), applied to a gesture that isn't an engine gesture at all.

apps/storybook-basics/src/hosts/blockAutoFit.ts — new. useAutoFitHeight: measures a Block's own header/footer chrome and its free members' real DOM rects, calls blockExpandedFitHeight, and carries a named reentrancy latch (applyingRef) modelled on Vyuh Flow's _isMovingGroupNodes/shouldSkipUpdates. Also owns measureKey — a live drag moves a descendant's position, which never wakes a ResizeObserver watching for size changes; without this key the parent does not track the child until release.

apps/storybook-basics/src/hosts/hostScene.ts — additive: HostNodeData.membersLayout/.autoFit (absent → today's "stack" behaviour, unchanged), and a second, dedicated DRAG_MEMBER_SCENE fixture — not an edit to the shared HOST_SCENE, which SceneHosts.stories.tsx's own assertions already pin.

apps/storybook-basics/src/hosts/nodeViews.tsx — additive: BlockNodeView wires the drag + fit hooks (called unconditionally, inert unless membersLayout: "free"), and moveMember writes a settled drag into SceneNode.position — that field's meaning for a parentId node was already documented at scene.ts:60-72 and never read or written until this lane.

apps/storybook-basics/src/stories/FitToContentHosts.stories.tsx — new, 4 stories, tagged area:blocks / lane:fit-to-content-hosts: a round trip (drag down, assert tracking + containment + convergence, drag back) for each host, plus a capture-only “Settled” variant per host that stops mid-fit so the screenshot shows the grown box rather than the fully-reset end state.
docs/ALGORITHM-PROVENANCE.md — new section for this lane's three files, including the two mutation tests (see Findings).
Zero files touched under src/components or src/scene — the concurrent skin-migration and polarity lanes' write sets were respected exactly; reactFlowHost.tsx and tldrawHost.tsx are also untouched.
findings: Both engines drag a free member with zero engine-specific code. The drag wrapper carries POINTER_OWNED_CLASS ("nodrag") — the SAME marker React Flow's own dragHandle filter and tldraw's own contentOwnsPress already both honor for the Code face and the Value capsule. Neither host file needed a single line added for member-dragging specifically to work; tldraw did not resist, contrary to what the brief flagged as a real possibility — checked directly rather than assumed, by writing the story and running it.

A real bug was caught mid-build, not hidden: the first working version tracked the parent correctly on drag END but NOT during the gesture — ResizeObserver fires on SIZE changes of the element it watches, and a live drag only ever changes a descendant's position. Mutation-verified: removing the measureKey argument from useAutoFitHeight and rerunning the exact same two stories reproduced the class of bug this whole feature exists to prevent — slot.bottom exceeded box.bottom mid-drag, i.e. the member started to walk past the wall while the gesture was still in flight. Restored, reverified green.

The reentrancy latch is real defensive code, verified NOT currently load-bearing — stated as exactly that, not oversold. Named after Vyuh Flow's _isMovingGroupNodes/shouldSkipUpdates (this lane's own prior-art report, card 6) and reactFlowHost.tsx's own prior NodeResizer defect (writing per-move fed back into XYResizer's gesture math and collapsed the node), the latch guards against a write-triggered ResizeObserver re-entering itself. Mutation-tested: this lane deleted the if (applyingRef.current) return line, reran both Drag A Member stories including the convergence assertion (the SAME box height, sampled two animation frames apart), and they still passed — because free members are position: absolute from a fixed region origin and the Block only ever grows downward, so re-measuring after any write finds IDENTICAL member rects. The latch is kept, named, and documented as verified-inert insurance for a future change (an upward-growing region, a header whose height depends on the Block's own height) that would silently reintroduce the exact bug class this repo has already shipped once.

The write-back destination for a member's position already existed and was never used. scene/scene.ts:60-72 already documents SceneNode.position, for a parentId node, as “the node's authored at-rest placement, in the PARENT's coordinate space… a host mid-drag owns the moving copy and writes back here at rest.” That sentence predates this lane by at least a day and nothing ever read or wrote it — free-layout dragging was contractually possible the whole time, just unwired.

Fit-during-drag, not fit-at-settle — and why: the fit height recomputes continuously while the gesture is in flight (driven by measureKey), because Zach's ask is explicitly about the parent redrawing itself “automatically” during the drag, not just afterward, and the acceptance test samples 5 intermediate points and asserts containment at every one, not only at the end. The member's OWN scene position is still written once, at release — splitting “what renders live” from “what gets recorded” is what keeps an aborted or jittery drag from leaving a half-finished write in a story or an undo stack to reconcile.

Baseline preserved exactly: tsc clean before and after; pnpm exec vitest --project=unit 38 files / 721 tests, byte-identical; pnpm test-stories 59 → 60 files, 258 → 262 tests (the 4 new stories), every pre-existing story unchanged — confirming the “inert unless membersLayout is set” claim isn't just asserted in a comment. Reran the two round-trip stories 4 times back-to-back with no flake.

sections.heading: Owed wiring — what a component-owning lane has to do
sections.html:
One item, stated with the exact change, not a direction.

FileChangeWhy it cannot be done from here
src/components/blockMembers.tsxGive free layout its own drag mechanism — the exact shape hosts/memberDrag.ts's useFreeMemberDrag already is — as a real BlockMembersProps.onMembersChange counterpart to what stack layout's dnd-kit boundary already does. Today free's own slotStyle branch is a bare position: absolute with zero pointer listeners; every consumer that wants free-layout dragging (not just this app's own hosts) has to reimplement it outside the component, which is exactly the trap this repo's core rule (“interaction geometry is host-owned”) is meant to prevent for a gesture that is actually BOUNDED to one component's own box, not the canvas.A skin-migration lane owns src/components/** this session (trace.tsx, block.tsx, badge.tsx, port.tsx, portEdge.tsx, traceTerminal.tsx all live). Moving this hook in now would collide with in-flight edits to files this lane never touched.

sections.heading: What could not be verified
sections.html:
• A third host was not tried. The claim “both hosts drag it with zero engine-specific code” is verified for React Flow and tldraw, the two engines this app ships; nothing here proves the same is true of an engine that intercepts pointer events differently (Konva, a plain SVG canvas, etc.).
  • Width was not exercised, only height. blockExpandedFitHeight only ever returns a height; fitBoxToMembers (the layout lane's own function) also returns a width, but this lane's demo drags a member DOWN only — dragging one to the right, growing the parent's width, was not built or measured here.
  • No stress test for many simultaneous free members. The fixture has two; the fit math itself is unit-tested against larger member lists by the prior lane's fitToContent.test.ts, but this lane's own host-level story does not exercise more than two DOM elements moving at once.
  • Performance under a real high-frequency pointer stream was not profiled. dragSteps samples 5 evenly-spaced points; a real mouse fires far more pointermove events per second, and whether the measure-and-re-render cost per event stays imperceptible at that rate was not measured, only reasoned about (the whole computation is a handful of getBoundingClientRect calls, not a layout of many nodes).
